newsitem.title: UK: Ex-Barings boss loses London court claim for bonus.
newsitem.headline: Ex-Barings boss loses London court claim for bonus.

text.p: A former boss of rogue trader Nick Leeson lost her claim for a 500,000 pound ($800,000) bonus from Barings bank which collapsed two years ago under a mountain of debt, Britain's Press Association news agency said on Thursday.
American-born Mary Walz said she was promised the bonus on the day before Barings ran into crisis because of losses from Leeson's huge unauthorised dealings in Asia.
Walz, who lives in London, told PA that her case before an industrial tribunal in the British capital had failed.

"I put the question before the tribunal for the very obvious purpose of seeking its independent review and to attempt to isolate what was strictly an employment issue from the complexities of the tragedy of the collapse of Barings," she told the news agency.
"Having put the question to the tribunal, I now accept and respect its decision."

Walz who was in charge of setting up a Barings operation in Hong Kong, was dismissed when Dutch company Internationale Nederlanden Group (ING) took over the failed bank. Leeson, who was based in Singapore, was also under her direction.

She told the tribunal in October that Barings' bosses had told her the bonus was "set in stone". But the bank said the profit-related bonus scheme became non-existent when its profits disappeared almost overnight.
Barings' losses were estimated at around 1.4 billion pounds.
Walz, 36, is one of nine former directors accused of negligence in a lawsuit filed by Barings' auditors. She was also criticised in a report into the bank's collapse.
Leeson is currently serving 6-1/2 years in a Singapore prison for his part in Barings' demise. ($1=.6161 Pound)
